Father '''James Cullen''', [[Society of Jesus|S.J.]] (19 April 1867 &ndash; 7 December 1933) was an Irish mathematician. 

He was born at 89 West Street, [[Drogheda]], County Louth, to Michael Cullen, a baker, and Catherine McDonough.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/e8640c3917108|title=General Registrar's Office|last=|first=|date=|website=IrishGenealogy.ie|publisher=|access-date=19 April 2017}}</ref> Initially, he was educated privately, then by the Christian Brothers.<ref>[http://www.fermatsearch.org/history/cullenbio.html Fr James Cullen SJ - Biography] Fermat Search.</ref> He studied pure and applied mathematics at [[Trinity College, Dublin]], then at Mungret College, Limerick, before deciding to become a [[Jesuit]]. He studied in England in Mansera House, and St. Mary's, and was ordained as a priest on 31 July 1901.<ref name=tablet/>

In 1905, he taught mathematics at [[Mount St Mary's College, Spinkhill]] in [[Derbyshire]] and published his finding of what is now known as [[Cullen number]]s in [[number theory]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Keller | first = Wilfrid
 | doi = 10.2307/2153382
 | issue = 212
 | journal = Mathematics of Computation
 | mr = 1308456
 | pages = 1733–1741, S39–S46
 | title = New Cullen primes
 | volume = 64
 | year = 1995| doi-access = free
 }} With a biographical sketch of James Cullen by T. G. Holt and a supplement by Keller and Wolfgang Niebuhr.</ref>

He ended up looking after accounts for the English province of the Jesuits, while contributing to mathematics journals.<ref name=tablet>{{cite news|url=http://archive.thetablet.co.uk/article/16th-december-1933/24/obituary|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817110637/http://archive.thetablet.co.uk/article/16th-december-1933/24/obituary|archive-date=2016-08-17|url-status=dead|newspaper=The Tablet|date=16 December 1933|title=The Rev., J. Cullen, S.J.|department=Obituaries}}</ref>
